h1: The 7 Best M-Audio Studio Monitors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best M-Audio Studio Monitors: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 M-Audio studio monitors from the BX3 to the Forty Eighty, compared on woofer size, power, DSP and wired versus Bluetooth.
summary: The M-Audio BX5BT is the studio monitor to buy for a typical desk: 5 inch drivers, DSP room tuning and app control, plus Bluetooth for casual listening. The wired BX4 is the cleaner pick for pure monitoring, the Forty Sixty adds 6.5 inch woofers and 100W for bigger rooms, and the BX3 is the entry price. The Forty Eighty is the 8 inch step for low-end work.
intro: M-Audio's lineup looks like a ladder of woofer sizes, but the more important split is wired versus Bluetooth. A studio monitor exists to tell you the truth about a mix, and a wireless link adds a codec and a delay between your DAW and the speaker. That is fine for background music and a poor idea for tracking or editing, which is why the BX line sells both versions at different prices.

We ranked seven models on the Primea framework, weighting woofer size against room size, input type, room-tuning features and price. The spec sheets give driver diameters and, for the Forty series, power in watts, so the ranking is built on those and on what each connection method means for a desktop studio.

products.name: M-AUDIO BX5BT 5" Desktop Studio Monitors Pair
products.verdict: 5 inch desktop monitors with built-in DSP room tuning, app control and Bluetooth.
products.description:
The BX5BT pairs 5 inch drivers with built-in DSP tuning for your room, plus app control to fine-tune the sound and Bluetooth for wireless playback.

It wins because the DSP is the feature other budget monitors lack. A desk against a wall boosts bass and smears the low end, and DSP room correction lets you tame it without foam or a rebuild. At 5 inches the woofer is bigger than the BX3 and BX4, which gives more low-end authority.

Buy it for a home studio on a typical desk. The caveat is that the spec sheet lists no power figure, and the Bluetooth link should not be used for tracking.
products.idealFor: Home studios on a typical desk, especially in a room with poor acoustics.
products.skipIf: You want a pure wired monitor with no wireless extras.

products.name: M-AUDIO BX4 4.5" Wired Studio Monitors Pair
products.verdict: 4.5 inch kevlar woofers on a latency-free wired connection.
products.description:
The BX4 uses 4.5 inch kevlar woofers and a wired connection that the maker describes as latency free. It is sold as a pair, and aimed at upgrading built-in computer audio.

It ranks second because wired is the correct connection for monitoring, and it costs the same $100 to $200 as the Bluetooth BX5BT without the wireless link. It falls behind the BX5BT because it has no DSP room tuning and a slightly smaller driver.

Buy it for editing, mixing and tracking at a desk. The caveat is that the listing gives no power rating or tuning controls.
products.idealFor: Desktop producers who want a straightforward wired monitor for mixing.
products.skipIf: You want room correction or Bluetooth.

products.name: M-AUDIO Forty Sixty 6.5" Studio Monitor Speaker
products.verdict: A 6.5 inch kevlar woofer and 100W of power for bigger rooms.
products.description:
The Forty Sixty has a 6.5 inch kevlar woofer and is rated at 100W. It is the first step up from the BX desktop line, and priced $100 to $200.

The larger woofer moves more air, which is the physical reason for deeper, steadier low end at a given volume. It ranks third because the listing says speaker, not pair, so confirm how many you receive, and because a 6.5 inch cabinet needs more desk or stand space.

Buy it for a larger room or when bass accuracy matters. The caveat is the quantity ambiguity in the listing.
products.idealFor: Producers in a larger room who want deeper, more controlled low end.

products.name: M-AUDIO BX3 3.5" Wired Studio Monitors Pair
products.verdict: 3.5 inch kevlar woofers, wired, at $50 to $100, the cheapest M-Audio pair here.
products.description:
The BX3 uses 3.5 inch kevlar woofers over a latency-free wired connection, sold as a pair at $50 to $100. It is aimed at upgrading built-in computer speakers.

It ranks fourth because 3.5 inches cannot reach as low as the larger models, so bass-heavy music will need headphones for checking. It is the right size for a small desk and costs half what the BX5BT does.

Buy it for light production and desk listening. The caveat is limited low end.
products.idealFor: Beginners on a small desk who want to move beyond laptop speakers.

products.name: M-AUDIO Forty Eighty 8" Studio Monitor Speaker
products.verdict: An 8 inch kevlar woofer and 150W, the biggest and most expensive M-Audio here.
products.description:
The Forty Eighty has an 8 inch kevlar woofer and is rated at 150W, priced $200 to $500. It is the top of this lineup.

It ranks fifth for most buyers because 8 inch monitors need room: in a small bedroom studio the bass overloads the space and your mixes suffer. In a larger treated room, it has the most headroom of the group.

Buy it for a bigger space or bass-driven genres. The caveat is that, like the Forty Sixty, the listing says speaker and not pair.
products.idealFor: Producers in a large or treated room working with bass-heavy music.
products.skipIf: Your room is small or untreated.

products.name: M-AUDIO BX4BT 4.5" Bluetooth Studio Monitors Pair
products.verdict: The BX4 with Bluetooth added, for wireless playback from a phone or laptop.
products.description:
The BX4BT shares the BX4's 4.5 inch kevlar woofers and adds Bluetooth pairing. It is sold as a pair at $100 to $200.

It ranks sixth because Bluetooth is the feature you pay for and the one a studio should avoid for critical work, and it has no DSP like the BX5BT. It makes sense for a producer who also uses the speakers to play music.

Buy it for mixed use. The caveat is that wireless adds delay.
products.idealFor: Producers who also want the speakers for casual listening.
products.skipIf: You only monitor, in which case the wired BX4 is better.

products.name: M-AUDIO BX3BT 3.5" Bluetooth Studio Monitors Pair
products.verdict: 3.5 inch woofers with Bluetooth, the smallest wireless option in the lineup.
products.description:
The BX3BT has the BX3's 3.5 inch kevlar woofers with Bluetooth, priced $100 to $200 as a pair.

It ranks last because it costs more than the wired BX3 for a feature studio work does not want, and it still has the small driver's limited low end. It earns a place as the smallest wireless pair for a compact desk.

Buy it if wireless matters more than studio accuracy. The caveat is price.
products.idealFor: A compact desk where you want wireless playback and basic monitoring.
products.skipIf: You want studio accuracy at the lowest price.

whatMatters.detail: Bigger woofers move more air and reach lower, but they overload small rooms. The BX3 at 3.5 inches suits a tiny desk, the BX5BT at 5 inches a typical bedroom, the Forty Eighty at 8 inches a large room. Match driver size to the room before looking at price.

Bluetooth adds delay and compression between your computer and the speaker, which hurts tracking and editing. Wired models such as the BX3 and BX4 are described as latency free. Use Bluetooth only for casual listening, and wired for anything where timing and accuracy matter.

A desk near a wall exaggerates bass. The BX5BT lists built-in DSP and app control to tune the speaker to the room. It will not replace acoustic treatment, but it reduces boominess that would otherwise mislead your mixes. Look for the word DSP in the listing.

Wattage indicates headroom, not loudness alone. The Forty Sixty lists 100W and the Forty Eighty 150W. The BX line does not list power on these listings. More headroom means less distortion at reference volume, which matters in a larger room.

Stereo mixing needs two speakers. The BX models are listed as pairs, but the Forty Sixty and Forty Eighty are listed as a speaker. Confirm the quantity in the listing and the cart before buying, since a single monitor costs half but leaves you with one channel.

faq.q: Do I need an audio interface?
faq.a: Studio monitors need a clean source. The BX models are described as wired and designed to upgrade computer audio, but check the listing for input types. A bundle with an interface is a separate product and not part of this ranking.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with studio monitors?
faq.a: Buying too big. An 8 inch Forty Eighty in a small bedroom overloads the room and misleads your mixes. Choose a BX3 or BX5BT for small rooms, and step up only if the space can handle the bass.

faq.q: Is the BX5BT worth it over the BX4?
faq.a: Yes if your room is untreated. The BX5BT adds DSP room tuning, app control and 5 inch drivers, while the BX4 is a plain wired pair with 4.5 inch woofers. Both cost $100 to $200.

faq.q: How do I set up the speakers?
faq.a: Place them at ear height, forming an equilateral triangle with your head, and keep them away from walls where possible. The BX5BT's app can then fine-tune the response for the room.

faq.q: Can the Bluetooth models be used for mixing?
faq.a: They can, but the wireless link adds delay and compression. Use the wired input where available, and treat Bluetooth on the BX4BT and BX3BT as a convenience for background music.

faq.q: Do I get two speakers with the Forty Sixty?
faq.a: The listing says speaker, not pair, so confirm in the cart. If you receive one, you need to buy a second for stereo. The BX models are sold as pairs.

finalTake: The M-AUDIO BX5BT 5" Desktop Studio Monitors Pair is the best M-Audio monitor for most home studios thanks to DSP room tuning and app control, with the wired BX4 as the cleaner alternative. Choose the BX3 on a tight budget, the Forty Sixty for bigger rooms and the Forty Eighty for large treated spaces. Always confirm whether you are buying a pair or a single speaker.
